days.title: Easy + relaxed strides + Strength A
days.desc: 6 miles total at conversational effort. Let pace follow recovery and conditions; do not force a fixed 9:30 pace. If recovered and pain-free, include 4 × 15 seconds of relaxed, quick running near the end, with 60–90 seconds walking/jogging between. Strides are smooth, not sprints, and stay inside the daily mileage. Strength A after Tuesday: split squat 6–8/side, push-up 6–12, single-leg glute bridge 8–12/side, straight-knee calf raise 10–15/side, side plank 20–30 sec/side. One set for the first two full weeks, then two sets; finish each with 2–3 good reps left. Add backpack/dumbbell load when the top of the range is smooth. Do not lift to failure or chase soreness. Added distance stays easy; do not add faster repetitions. Shorten this run if recovery or normal running mechanics deteriorate.

days.title: Optional walk + mobility
days.desc: Optional 20–30 min gentle walk or easy bike, RPE 1–2. Then 5 minutes of comfortable ankle and hip mobility. Skip if tired.

days.title: Goal-pace introduction — 2 × 5 minutes
days.desc: 7 miles total: start with 1.5 miles easy, then 2 × 5 minutes at 8:23–8:35/mi with 3 minutes easy jogging between. Run the remaining distance easy. This replaces the planned pickups; do not add extra repetitions. Goal pace must feel controlled, roughly RPE 5–6/10, with relaxed mechanics. Use this session only if recovered, pain-free and the preceding two weeks were consistent. If breathing becomes hard, form deteriorates or effort rises above controlled, slow down or finish easy; do not force 8:23. All recoveries and warm-up/cool-down miles are included in the daily total. Strength B after Thursday: row or assisted pull-up 6–12, dead bug 6–8/side, side plank 20–30 sec/side. Two controlled sets. On easy Thursdays only, add one or two sets of step-up 6–8/side, hamstring bridge walkout 4–6, and bent-knee calf raise 10–15/side. On quality Thursdays skip the extra lower-body work. In taper, reduce to one light set; no hard leg lifting in race week. Treat this as an all-easy 7-mile run if the October 26 mileage increase has not fully settled; goal-pace practice can wait.

Keep your stride relaxed and let the recovery jog reset your breathing. If still fatigued or the pace feels hard early, finish the remaining mileage at 9:45/mi if comfortable.

days.title: Rest before the long run
days.desc: Run 0 miles. Optional 15–20 minute walk at RPE 1–2 out of 10. Set out your shoes, water and familiar fuel for Saturday.

days.title: Easy long run
days.desc: Run 8 miles at 9:45/mi on flat ground, with hills paced by conversational effort. Run 8 easy miles on a familiar route. Finish feeling like you could comfortably keep going. Stop at 3 hours even if you have mileage left.

days.title: Rest after the long run
days.desc: Run 0 miles. Optional 15–25 minute relaxed walk. Check how your legs feel on stairs and use Monday as rest if walking still feels unusually hard.

days.title: Race-week rest
days.desc: Run 0 miles. Take normal walks and 5 minutes of gentle mobility if it helps you feel loose. Skip hard strength and save your legs for Sunday.

days.title: Easy aerobic run
days.desc: Run 4 miles at 9:45/mi. Start the first mile at 10:10/mi, then settle into a pace where you can speak in full sentences. Keep the last mile easy and skip heavy lifting.

days.title: Race-week rest
days.desc: Run 0 miles. Take normal walks and 5 minutes of gentle mobility if it helps you feel loose. Skip hard strength and save your legs for Sunday.

days.title: 2 × 0.5 mile at marathon pace
days.desc: Warm up for 1 miles at 9:45/mi. Run 2 × 0.5 mile at 8:01/mi. Jog 0.25 mile at 10:10/mi between reps. Cool down for 0.75 miles at 9:45/mi. Finish fresh and keep the rest of the day easy. If still fatigued or the pace feels hard early, finish the remaining mileage at 9:45/mi if comfortable.

days.title: Race-week rest
days.desc: Run 0 miles. Take normal walks and 5 minutes of gentle mobility if it helps you feel loose. Skip hard strength and save your legs for Sunday.

days.title: Optional race shakeout
days.desc: Run 2 flat miles at 10:00/mi. Keep the first mile at 10:10/mi and finish relaxed. Take full rest instead if you feel more comfortable resting before a race.

days.title: Austin Marathon
days.desc: Run 26.2 miles. Open miles 1–3 around 8:07/mi on flat ground and keep climbs controlled. Settle near 8:00/mi on flatter miles through mile 20, using even effort on climbs and descents. Aim to pass halfway near 1:45. After mile 20, hold your rhythm if you can still run smoothly. Use official mile markers and elapsed time to check pacing. Start your practiced fueling early and follow the same schedule you rehearsed.

strength.A: Strength A after Tuesday: split squat 6–8/side, push-up 6–12, single-leg glute bridge 8–12/side, straight-knee calf raise 10–15/side, side plank 20–30 sec/side. One set for the first two full weeks, then two sets; finish each with 2–3 good reps left. Add backpack/dumbbell load when the top of the range is smooth. Do not lift to failure or chase soreness.
strength.B: Strength B after Thursday: row or assisted pull-up 6–12, dead bug 6–8/side, side plank 20–30 sec/side. Two controlled sets. On easy Thursdays only, add one or two sets of step-up 6–8/side, hamstring bridge walkout 4–6, and bent-knee calf raise 10–15/side. On quality Thursdays skip the extra lower-body work. In taper, reduce to one light set; no hard leg lifting in race week.

progressionRule: Advance only after recovering normally from your recent mileage and long run. Repeat or reduce the last well-tolerated week after several missed runs or persistent fatigue. Keep Friday and Sunday as rest days except on race day. Keep Saturday long runs and one structured quality session per week. Keep January 14 easy before the January 16 race rehearsal. Cap long runs at three hours and begin the taper January 25 even if the peak is shortened.
qualityRule: Warm-ups, recovery jogs and cool-downs are included in the stated mileage. Do the faster blocks when easy effort and recovery have been normal. If not, run easy at the same or shorter distance.

checkpoints.title: Cutback pace check
checkpoints.review: Record the effort and next-day recovery from the steady miles. Keep the next set of reps controlled.

checkpoints.title: 3:30 readiness review
checkpoints.review: Review your consistency, January 16 rehearsal and fueling. Keep 3:30 as your A goal if 8:04/mi felt controlled late in the long run and you recovered normally.

racePreparation.trainingPriority: Consistent weeks and recovery take priority over hitting a higher peak number. Keep long runs mostly easy; practice controlled goal-pace blocks only when readiness conditions are met.
racePreparation.fuelPractice: For runs lasting 1–2.5 hours, build toward 30–60 g carbohydrate per hour using familiar products. For longer race-duration efforts, higher intakes may help but require gradual gut training and individual tolerance; never introduce an untested intake on race day.
racePreparation.goalReview: Use late-December/January training, a suitable tune-up race if available, and long-run recovery to review the A goal. Shorter-race equivalence is supportive evidence only; marathon endurance and fueling must also support the target.

goalPaceProgression.workout: 3 miles at marathon pace during taper
